messages:
IncidentBot: [ALERT] 03:12 UTC — pool 'us-west-2:pool-paged-kv' high OOM churn: 87% recent containers OOMKilled. Sample error: "CUDA out of memory"; CGroup reports kill. Dash: https://grafana.redwood/alert/kv-frag. Paging oncall.
Alice M: grabbing logs and taking initial coord. Oncall here.
Ben R: runtime checking. Looks like paged-attention allocator resident set steadily increased across several hosts; fragmentation metric spiked ~3x over ~5h. Likely small-hole accumulation in KV pages preventing contiguous allocations.
Clara S: customer impact: two tenants in us-west-2 seeing 500s on chat endpoints since ~02:45 UTC. Support Ops looped in.
Support Ops: confirmed affected tenants: tenant-alpha, tenant-echo. Notifying account teams. We'll draft a short status update if mitigation ETA > 15m.
Diego V: pasted node-level excerpt:
```
[2026-03-15T02:57:09Z] paged_alloc: allocate_contiguous failed: insufficient contiguous slab
[2026-03-15T02:57:09Z] kv: live_prefixes=1243 frag_pct=0.69 resident=1.35G
[2026-03-15T02:57:12Z] cuda: cuMemAlloc returned OOM (2)
[2026-03-15T02:57:12Z] kernel: cgroup: kill -9 pid 23456 (inference)
```
Alice M: any config changes recently? batcher or prefix retention jobs?
Ben R: there was a batcher tweak that increased prefix retention across batches rolled at ~02:05. That could make prefixes persist longer and increase fragmentation over time. Also we didn't have aggressive KV eviction for this pool.
Alice M: OK. Need quick mitigation to stop customer impact: options?
Ben R: mitigation options ranked:
- immediate: drain + restart hottest nodes (fast, disruptive per node)
- mid: temporarily route traffic to smaller model variant (gpt-medium-quant) using smart-routing (lower perf but avoids OOM)
- config: bump KV eviction aggressiveness (short-term reclaim)
- experimental: enable defrag pass (CPU heavy, risky on-prod)
Clara S: start with drain+restart for 3 hotspot nodes + canary config bump for eviction. That keeps most traffic live.
InfraBot: automation available: `infractl node drain --pool=pool-paged-kv --nodes=node-uw2-12,node-uw2-14 --grace=20s`
Alice M: executing drain on node-uw2-12 and node-uw2-14 now. Routing will shift to backups and cross-region if necessary.
Ben R: I'm pushing an emergency toggle to reduce live prefix age: kv.max_live_prefix_age_ms 600000->300000 and increase eviction scan frequency. Will push to 2 canary nodes first.
Diego V: observed an OOM on node-uw2-16 during the first drain attempt; queued that for restart too.
Support Ops: posted initial customer notice: "Degraded responses/500s for chat endpoints in us-west-2. Engineers mitigating. Next update in 15 minutes."
Ben R: canary push at 03:18 UTC looks good: eviction count up, fragmentation declined on canary nodes. No latency regressions in request tail.
Clara S: good. Roll to whole pool if metrics stable for 3m.
Alice M: rolling restart initiated for node-uw2-12, node-uw2-14, node-uw2-16. Infra routing moved small fraction to us-east-1 per fallback policy.
InfraBot: routing change: applied cross-region overflow for pool; spare capacity limited. Warning sent to autoscale team.
Diego V: post-restart memory resident dropped ~650MB on each restarted node. Service container restarts decreased from 8/min to ~1/min on affected hosts.
Support Ops: smoke tests for tenant-alpha/echo show success rate improved to 98-99% post-mitigation. Two intermittent 500s remain; monitoring.
Clara S: assign follow-ups: create post-incident ticket to investigate allocator fragmentation root cause and schedule engineering work: defrag pass + KV freelist improvements + telemetry for per-page hole maps.
Ben R: I'll capture allocator heap dumps, hole maps, and a workload trace for repro. Initial hypothesis: batcher change increased prefix lifetime -> slow accumulation of micro-fragments -> inability to satisfy contiguous requests triggering OOMs.
Alice M: documented immediate remediation steps in incident runbook. Next steps: 1) finish rolling restart of identified hotspots 2) propagate eviction changes to pool if canary remains stable 3) ensure customer comms updated 4) create INC ticket and assign to eng.
Clara S: taking ownership of the postmortem and handoff. Please include timelines for: frag ratio increase, eviction rate, restart timestamps, customer 500 counts.
Ben R: noted. I'll own the engineering fix (allocator compaction + telemetry). Est. fix timeline: spike to mid-term (2-4 weeks) for safe rollout.
Alice M: closing active mitigation — monitoring mode. Metrics stable for 12m. Creating incident INC-2026-0456 and linking artifacts.
IncidentBot: Incident INC-2026-0456 created by Alice M — severity P2 — status: mitigated -> monitoring. Next update scheduled in 4h.
Clara S: handoff complete. Will run deeper analysis during next shift. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Alice M: thanks team, great quick work. End of thread and handing to Clara S for follow-up.
